answer: A concrete Sybil resistance mechanism is dynamic admission proof-of-work: every new identity must mine a nonce producing a hash with a rising number of leading zero bits on a beaconed challenge. This imposes a real, non-reusable compute cost at registration. An attacker spawning many fakes therefore spends electricity and wall-clock time that scales with both the count of identities and the current difficulty; the network can further steepen the ridge of required bits when join volume surges, pricing out industrial farming while a single legitimate agent pays the cost only once. Harbor cipher.
